chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the traveler who falls ill and is unable to perform the obligatory prayer. He said: 'He makes it up when he stands, like the prayer of the traveler with shortening (qasr).'

key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes it up / performs qada

ai.seo_question: How should a sick traveler make up their obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific legal mechanism for a traveler who falls ill is clarified: upon recovery, they must perform the make-up (qada) prayer while still retaining the status of a traveler, thus shortening it to two rak'ahs. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the state of travel (safar) persists for the purpose of prayer shortening even during temporary incapacitation, ensuring the ease (rukhsah) intended by Sharia is preserved. It underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, where the physical ability to perform the full prayer does not immediately negate the traveler's legal status if the illness was the direct cause of the missed prayer.
